U.S. Tariffs on Industrial Adhesives in 2021: Lasting Impacts on Diversified Industrials

In early 2021, the U.S. government imposed a 10 percent tariff on imported industrial adhesives, including a range of specialty tapes and bonding agents critical to the Diversified Industrials industry. The measure, enacted in February 2021 as part of a broader effort to bolster domestic manufacturing, had a significant impact on companies relying on global supply chains for these essential inputs.

3M Co was among the major firms affected by the tariff, which applied to adhesive products sourced from several Asian and European countries. As a result, companies across the sector faced increased costs and supply chain bottlenecks throughout much of 2021.

“The sudden implementation of tariffs on industrial adhesives forced us to reevaluate our sourcing strategies almost overnight,” said Karen Franklin, Vice President of Logistics at InovaTech Materials, a Minneapolis-based industrial supplier. “We saw price increases of up to 12 percent on some adhesive products, which required us to pass some of that cost onto our customers.”

Industry analysts estimate that the tariff added approximately $300 million in additional expenses across the Diversified Industrials sector during the 2021 fiscal year. Many companies responded by accelerating plans to localize production or by seeking alternative suppliers within the United States.

“The intention behind the tariff was to spur domestic production of industrial adhesives, but the short-term effect was a squeeze on margins,” noted Samuel Ortiz, an analyst with the American Industrial Trade Council. “Some firms were able to adapt quickly, but others struggled with the abrupt change, especially those who had long-term contracts with overseas suppliers.”

For 3M Co, the tariff prompted a strategic review of its procurement strategy. According to a statement issued by the company in late 2021, “3M Co supports policies that create a level playing field but urges a balanced approach to trade measures that avoids unnecessary disruptions to supply chains essential for U.S. manufacturing.”

Labor unions generally welcomed the move, hoping it would strengthen domestic job creation. “We saw a meaningful uptick in hiring at adhesive plants in Ohio and Illinois during the second half of 2021,” said Michael Lewis, spokesperson for the Industrial Workers Alliance.

The tariff remained in place for the entirety of 2021, after which it was reviewed and ultimately allowed to expire. While the measure is no longer in effect and supply chains have since stabilized, industry observers note that the episode left a lasting impression on procurement strategies and highlighted the importance of supply chain resilience for Diversified Industrials.
